rows.question: Do I need to touch out on the bus?
rows.answer:
No – on a bus you only need to **touch in** when you board; there is no touch‑out required.  

Source: TfL “Touching in and out” guidance – “On a bus or tram you only need to touch in.”【https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/how-to-pay-and-where-to-buy-tickets-and-oyster/pay-as-you-go/touching-in-and-out】

rows.question: What happens if I forget to tap out at the end of my Tube journey?
rows.answer:
If you forget to tap out, TfL can’t work out the correct fare, so it will charge you the **maximum fare** for that journey. That charge does not count toward any daily or weekly fare cap, and if you repeatedly fail to touch in or out you could be issued a penalty fare or even face prosecution.  

Source: [Touching in and out – What happens if you don’t touch in and out](https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/how-to-pay-and-where-to-buy-tickets-and-oyster/pay-as-you-go/touching-in-and-out)

rows.question: Can I pay for the Tube with Google Pay on my phone?
rows.answer:
Yes – you can use Google Pay on your phone (or other compatible devices) to pay for the Tube. Mobile payments work the same way as a contactless card: just tap your device on the yellow reader when you touch in and out.  

Source: [Pay as you go – Pay as you go with mobile](https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/how-to-pay-and-where-to-buy-tickets-and-oyster/pay-as-you-go/contactless-and-mobile-pay-as-you-go) (section “Pay as you go with mobile”).

rows.question: My Tube was 20 minutes late. Can I get a refund?
rows.answer:
Yes – you can claim a refund because a Tube journey delayed ≥ 15 minutes qualifies for a service‑delay refund. You must submit the claim within 28 days of the delay (most refunds are processed automatically after about 48 hours).  

You can apply online via TfL’s “Apply for service delay refund” page: https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/refunds-and-replacements. If you used an Oyster card or contactless payment, check your journey history there and follow the instructions to request the refund.

rows.question: How does the Hopper fare work?
rows.answer: The Hopper fare gives you unlimited bus and tram journeys made within one hour of your first touch‑in for a single £1.75 adult pay‑as‑you‑go charge (the same discount applies to reduced‑rate fares). You must touch in with the same Oyster card or contactless device on each journey; if the card has a negative balance after the first trip, the Hopper fare won’t apply and you’ll need to top up within the hour to be eligible【https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/find-fares/bus-and-tram-fares】.

rows.question: Which lines run the Night Tube?
rows.answer:
The Night Tube runs on the **Central, Jubilee, Northern, Piccadilly, Victoria and Waterloo & City** lines on Friday and Saturday nights.  

Source: [The Night Tube – Overview](https://tfl.gov.uk/modes/tube/night-tube)

rows.question: Can people over 60 travel free in London?
rows.answer:
Yes – anyone aged 60 or over who lives in a London borough can apply for a **60+ London Oyster photocard**, which gives free travel on the Tube, bus, tram, DLR, London Overground and the Elizabeth line (except the West Drayton – Reading section) and on most National Rail services in London. 【https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/free-and-discounted-travel/60-plus-oyster-photocard】.  

The photocard is available until you become eligible for a Freedom Pass, and you must be a resident of a London borough to qualify.

rows.question: Does my 8 year old need a ticket for the Tube?
rows.answer:
No – an 8‑year‑old can travel for free on the Tube when they’re with a fare‑paying adult (up to four children under 11 per adult). They don’t need a ticket or a photocard.  

Source: TfL – “5‑10 Zip Oyster photocard” – a fare‑paying adult can travel with up to 4 children under 11 free of charge【https://tfl.gov.uk/fares/free-and-discounted-travel/5-10-zip-oyster-photocard】.
